Master of Environmental Science – MEnvSc
Study a one-year Master’s to gain the knowledge and experience to tackle the planet’s pressing challenges as a skilled environmental scientist.
Overview
Study details
Requirements
People
Apply & contact
Resolve environmental issues
Environmental Science investigates issues like climate change, sea level rise, and the impacts of industries like agriculture and mining. Explore how humans connect with and change the natural environment. Apply a science focus with biology, chemistry, geography, data science, and physics.
Learn tools and techniques to mitigate the human impact on the environment. Analyse complex datasets, draw conclusions, and communicate your results. Learn outside the classroom, with fieldwork such as monitoring the quality of waterways, soil, or air. The information you gather could contribute to policy and regulatory change.
Designed with input from industry professionals, the MEnvSc gives you hands-on, practical experience. You’ll complete real-world projects to make industry connections and graduate career-ready.
Get the postgraduate handbook
Fill in the form to find out more about your study options in our Wellington Faculty of Science and Engineering Postgraduate Handbook.
Download the handbook
How you’ll study
Part one
You’ll study core courses in your first two trimesters.
Understand contemporary environmental science issues from an interdisciplinary perspective.
Look at both Aotearoa New Zealand and the rest of the world.
You’ll also develop the essential field and lab skills of an environmental scientist. You’ll do independent research on an environmental science topic.
You’ll also focus your study on an area of interest with additional elective courses. These can be from a range of approved courses covering fields such as:
biology
chemistry
geophysics
geology
statistics
social science
policy
Māori studies
law.
Other courses may be considered by the head of the school if they are relevant.
Part two
In Trimester 3, choose between completing either:
a placement with an employer
an applied research project.
If you choose to study the Environmental Science Placement and Project course, you will have the chance to spend eight weeks working with an environmental science organisation.
If you only complete part of the MEnvSc
If you complete Part 1 of the Master of Environmental Science and don’t continue on to Part 2, you’ll be awarded a Postgraduate Diploma in Science (Environmental Science).
If you complete 60 points of coursework, you can be awarded a Postgraduate Certificate in Science (Environmental Science).
Part-time study options
You can study for an MEnvSc part time for up to three years.
You will need to do around 20 hours of work a week. Take this into account if you are working.

Entry
Bachelor's degree with at least a B average in a relevant subject
Research an area that interests you
Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington is the country’s top-ranked university for intensity of high-quality research.
See our research performance and rankings.
As part of your Master’s study, you’ll learn from and work with highly qualified academic staff and professional researchers who undertake internationally recognised work.
Environmental Science staff.
Research institutes
You’ll also have access to knowledge from academics and from across the Faculty of Science and Engineering, through work placements and guest lectures.
This includes specialists from the:
New Zealand Climate Change Research Institute
Antarctic Research Centre.
Future careers
Aotearoa New Zealand needs scientifically trained graduates who can influence environmental decision-making. You’ll be able to facilitate the science-policy-practice process throughout government, private sectors, and the community.
Your focus on science gives you opportunities to work in science-related roles, such as:
environmental scientist
data and policy analyst
environmental planner
land adviser
conservation coordinator.
environmental consultant
environmental educator
resources manager.
Your Master's degree in Environmental Science can also set you up for intermediate to senior policy and research roles where specialised, in-depth analysis is important.
Environmental careers
Scholarships
You may be able to get a scholarship to help fund your studies.
We have postgraduate and doctoral scholarships available, as well as specialised scholarships for different groups and subject areas.
postgraduate and doctoral scholarships
search scholarships.
Applicable scholarships
Jan Heine Research Scholarship in Biodiversity and Restoration Ecology
Averil Brent Scholarship in Science.
Summer research scholarships
There are several summer scholarships available. These give you the opportunity to gain experience in research—with the added bonus of paid work over the summer trimester.
Each scholarship gives you experience working with established researchers on a specified project and an insight into what studying for a research degree entails.
Summer Scholars Scheme.
Financial support
You can get support to stay on top of your finances by downloading our money management resources or by meeting with one of our student finance advisers.
We can show you how to manage your student loan or allowance, and help you sort out your budget. For students facing financial difficulties, we can help you apply for support from the Hardship Fund. Depending on your situation, you might also be able to get government or community support.
Talk to a student finance adviser
Financing your study
Work opportunities
Work as a research assistant
You may be able to work as a research assistant while you study. These are fixed-term, short contracts where you assist an academic on a specific research project.
Work as a tutor
Postgraduate students can apply for positions as tutors and lab demonstrators for undergraduate courses. You'll hear about these jobs through the School as they become available.
Make industry connections
The MEnvSc has been created with input from industry professionals. It gives you hands-on experience with real-world projects to support you to engage with the industry.
The MEnvSc involves close interaction with:
city and regional councils
Zealandia eco-sanctuary
MetService
GNS Science
NIWA.
During your study, you’ll also learn from guest lecturers from government agencies and the business sector. This is an opportunity to hear from people practicing in this space already.
Study for a PhD
Master’s students who complete the 180-point MEnvSc and include the ENSC510 (research project) are able to apply to do a PhD.
Begin your career as a scientist or academic and complete a major piece of original research with a PhD.
About PhDs
Community
Postgraduate study at Victoria University of Wellington will help you build valuable relationships and networks with peers, University staff and future colleagues. You'll have opportunities to attend events, seminars, workshops and social functions.
The Postgraduate Students' Association can also give you information on study at the University and provides a voice for you on campus.
